title: Outlook: folder sharing respects organisation restrictions on Default and Anonymous permissions
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap target and distinguishes existing folder-permission controls from the undocumented restrictions the new feature will honour. One minor correction is needed: Microsoft's folder-permission article says Update for a new policy configuration, whereas the Cloud Policy overview says Create.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: For Exchange Online calendars, Default applies to authenticated organisational users without an explicit permission entry.
claims.quote: Default applies to authenticated users in the organization who don't have an explicit permission entry.

claims.claim: For Exchange Online calendars, Anonymous applies to unauthenticated callers without access through a calendar-sharing relationship.
claims.quote: Anonymous applies to callers who aren't authenticated and don't have access through a calendar-sharing relationship.

claims.claim: Microsoft gives AvailabilityOnly as the typical value for the calendar Default entry.
claims.quote: Default applies to authenticated users in the organization who don't have an explicit permission entry. Its typical value is AvailabilityOnly.

claims.claim: Microsoft gives None as the typical value for the calendar Anonymous entry.
claims.quote: Anonymous applies to callers who aren't authenticated and don't have access through a calendar-sharing relationship. Its typical value is None.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that increasing Anonymous above None can expose calendar information more broadly than intended.
claims.quote: Increasing Anonymous above None can expose calendar information more broadly than intended.

claims.claim: For Microsoft 365 Apps for business, Cloud Policy supports only privacy-control policy settings.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy configurations target users and can be scoped to selected groups.
claims.quote: On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups, or to users who anonymously access documents using Office for the web.

claims.claim: The existing restriction procedure requires enabling Turn off sharing recommendation.
claims.quote: Enable each of the following policies: [...] Turn off sharing recommendation

claims.claim: The existing restriction procedure requires enabling Do not allow users to change permissions on folders.
claims.quote: Enable each of the following policies: [...] Do not allow users to change permissions on folders

claims.claim: After creating a policy configuration and enabling the three settings, select Update.

claims.fix: Acknowledge the documentation difference in the control note: the folder-permission article says Update, but https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy says select Create for a new configuration, and Review and publish > Update when changing an existing configuration.

claims.claim: Set DWORD DisableEditPermissions and DisableEditDefaultUserPermissions to 1 under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Options\Folders.
claims.quote: Either directly or through Group Policy, set the value of the following registry entries to 1: [...] HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Options\Folders\DisableEditDefaultUserPermissions [...] set their type to DWORD (32-bit).
